newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher on CBOT spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher on CBOT spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher along with other U.S. wheat markets -- receiving a boost from a rally in CBOT corn and soybeans, traders said.
The rally was brought on by Pro Farmer's estimate of 1996 U.S. corn production at 8.2 billion bushels, markedly lower than USDA's August estimate for corn output of 8.69 billion.

But gains in MGE spring wheat were limited by the substantial amount of farmer selling of spring wheat over the weekend, traders said. Country hedge pressure was evident from the outset of Monday's session, traders said.
On the MGE's cash trading floor, 104 cars and 15 trains of spring wheat were offered.
"Receipts have definitely increased with harvest," a floor source said.

MGE spring wheat ended two to seven cents per bushel higher, with Sept up two cents at $4.68 a bushel. Dec gained 4-3/4 cents to close at $4.64-1/4, Dec gained at the expense of Sept as players rolled long positions out of the nearby month.
CIS bought one million Sept bushels and 500,000 Dec, traders said, while Term Commodities sold 1.3 Sept. Wilson bear-spread one million Dec/Sept at four cents per bushel.
MGE barley futures closed two to five cents per bushel higher, with September up two cents at $7.78.
